theory.intro: The tangent-chord angle — the angle between a tangent and a chord drawn from the point of contact — equals the angle in the alternate segment: the inscribed angle standing on the same chord from a point on the arc on the other side of the chord.
facts: The angle between a tangent and a chord at the point of contact equals the angle in the alternate segment: if $TA$ is a chord from the point of contact $T$, then the tangent-chord angle equals $\angle TBA$ for any point $B$ on the arc on the far side of $TA$.
The **alternate segment** is the segment on the opposite side of the chord from the tangent-chord angle being measured — not the segment next to it.

Each point of contact has two (supplementary) tangent-chord angles for a given chord, one on each side of the chord — only the angle in the segment on the OTHER side matches a given tangent-chord angle.
steps: Identify the point of contact, the tangent, and the chord that forms the tangent-chord angle.
Identify the alternate segment — the arc on the far side of the chord from the tangent-chord angle.
Set the tangent-chord angle equal to the inscribed angle in the alternate segment, then solve.

foundation.solution_text: $x = 50^{\circ}$ (angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)
$x = 44^{\circ}$ (angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)

$D$ lies in the alternate segment (the arc on the far side of chord $TA$ from the marked angle), so $\angle TDA$ is the angle in the alternate segment.
$\angle TDA = 56^{\circ}$ (angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)
$\angle TCA$ is in the same segment as the marked angle, so it is not equal to it.
$x = 58^{\circ}$ (angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)

$3x = 2x + 15^{\circ}$ (angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)
$x = 15^{\circ}$

$\angle TAB = 52^{\circ}$ (angle between the tangent and chord $TB$ equals the angle in the alternate segment, at $A$)
$TA = TB$ (given), so $\triangle TAB$ is isosceles
$\angle TBA = \angle TAB = 52^{\circ}$ (base angles of isosceles triangle)
$x + 52^{\circ} + 52^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle TAB$)
$x = 76^{\circ}$

development.solution_text:
The tangent-chord angle for $TA$ is $25^{\circ} + 38^{\circ} = 63^{\circ}$ (angle between the tangent and $TB$, plus $\angle BTA$)
$x = 63^{\circ}$ (angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)

$TA = TB$ (given), so $\triangle TAB$ is isosceles
$\angle TAB = \angle TBA$ (base angles of isosceles triangle)
$\angle TAB + \angle TBA + 64^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle TAB$)
$\angle TAB = \angle TBA = 58^{\circ}$
$x = 58^{\circ}$ (angle between the tangent and chord $TB$ equals the angle in the alternate segment, at $A$)

$4x - 10^{\circ} = 2x + 30^{\circ}$ (angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)
$2x = 40^{\circ}$
$x = 20^{\circ}$
Tangent-chord angle $= 4(20^{\circ}) - 10^{\circ} = 70^{\circ}$

$B$ lies on the arc on the far side of chord $TA$ from the marked $47^{\circ}$ angle, so $B$ is in the alternate segment
$x = 47^{\circ}$ (angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)
$x = 66^{\circ}$ (angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)

$\angle TAB = \alpha$ (angle between the tangent and chord $TB$ equals the angle in the alternate segment, at $A$)
$\angle TBA = \beta$ (angle between the tangent and chord $TA$ equals the angle in the alternate segment, at $B$)
$TA = TB$ (given), so $\triangle TAB$ is isosceles, and its base angles are equal
$\angle TAB = \angle TBA$
$\therefore \alpha = \beta$

mastery.solution_text:
$\alpha + \beta = 90^{\circ}$ (tangent is perpendicular to the radius $OT$)
$\alpha = 90^{\circ} - \beta$
$OT = OA$ (equal radii), so $\triangle OTA$ is isosceles
$\angle OAT = \angle OTA = \beta$ (base angles of isosceles triangle)
$\angle TOA = 180^{\circ} - 2\beta$ (angle sum of $\triangle OTA$)
$x = \frac{1}{2}\angle TOA$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, standing on the minor arc $TA$)
$x = \frac{1}{2}(180^{\circ} - 2\beta) = 90^{\circ} - \beta$
$\therefore \alpha = x$

$\angle CAB = 55^{\circ}$ (angle between the tangent and chord $CB$ equals the angle in the alternate segment, at $A$)
$\angle ACB = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$\angle ABC + \angle ACB + \angle CAB = 180^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$)
$\angle ABC = 180^{\circ} - 90^{\circ} - 55^{\circ}$
$\angle ABC = 35^{\circ}$

$3x = x + 40^{\circ}$ (angle between the tangent and chord $TB$ equals the angle in the alternate segment, at $C$)
$2x = 40^{\circ}$
$x = 20^{\circ}$
Tangent-chord angle $= 3(20^{\circ}) = 60^{\circ}$, so $\angle TAB = 60^{\circ}$
$TA = TB$ (given), so $\triangle TAB$ is isosceles
$\angle TBA = \angle TAB = 60^{\circ}$ (base angles of isosceles triangle)
$\angle ATB = 180^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle TAB$)
All three angles of $\triangle TAB$ are $60^{\circ}$, so $\triangle TAB$ is equilateral
